defect.description: Isinstance(self.log_output, TextIO) never matches a real file: typing.TextIO is not a base class of what open() returns (io.TextIOWrapper, or the io.BufferedWriter of the default os.devnull log), so stop() still leaves every file log open, as before; it should test io.IOBase (or for a close method).

review_items: Default os.devnull binary handle leaks because the TextIO/int checks don't match it
Caller-passed binary files are not closed due to the TextIO check (old hasattr close handled any file-like)
Exception in close() skips process terminate/wait
Double stop() calls os.close on an already-closed int fd, raising OSError
No test covers the TextIO close path
No test covers the default log_output=None path
votes.evidence_quote: Line 37's `isinstance(self.log_output, TextIO)` is `False` for it, and line 39's `isinstance(..., int)` is also `False`, so neither close branch executes.
votes.justification: The review flags the right check in stop() and the real devnull/binary-file leak. It misreads the cause, though: it assumes text-mode files from open() pass the TextIO check and are closed, calling that path 'safe'. The real defect is that typing.TextIO matches no real file object, so every file log leaks.
